snp4.16:1.1:
Ven. Sāriputta:
“Never before
have I seen
snp4.16:1.4: of a teacher with such lovely speech
snp4.16:1.5:
come, together with his following
from Tusita heaven,
snp4.16:2.1:
as the One with Eyes
who appears to the world with its devas,
snp4.16:2.4:
having arrived at delight
all alone.
snp4.16:3.1:
To that One Awakened—
unentangled, Such, un-
deceptive,
come with his following—
snp4.16:3.2: I have come desiring a question
snp4.16:4.3:
the root of a tree,
a cemetery,
snp4.16:5.2: how many are the fears there
snp4.16:6.1:
how many the dangers in the world
for the monk going the direction
he never has gone
snp4.16:7.1:
What should be
the ways of his speech?
snp4.16:7.2:
What should be
his range there of action?
snp4.16:8.3:
would he blow away
his own impurities
snp4.16:8.4:
as a silver smith,
those in molten silver?”
snp4.16:9.1:
The Buddha:
“I will tell you
as one who knows,
what is comfort
for one disaffected
if he’s resorting to a place remote,
snp4.16:9.3:
desiring self-awakening
in line with the Dhamma.
snp4.16:10.1:
An enlightened monk,
living circumscribed,
mindful,
shouldn’t fear the five fears:
snp4.16:11.1:
shouldn’t be fazed
by those following another’s teaching
snp4.16:11.2:
even on seeing their manifold
threats;
snp4.16:11.4:
further dangers
as he seeks what is skillful.
snp4.16:12.1:
Touched
by the touch
of disease, hunger,
snp4.16:12.2:
he should endure cold
& inordinate heat.
snp4.16:12.3:
He with no home,
in many ways touched by these things,
snp4.16:12.4: striving, should make firm his persistence.
snp4.16:13.1:
He shouldn’t commit a theft,
shouldn’t speak a lie,
snp4.16:13.2:
should touch with thoughts of goodwill
beings firm & infirm.
snp4.16:13.3:
Conscious of when
his mind is stirred up & turbid,
snp4.16:13.4:
he should dispel it:
‘It’s on the side
of the Dark One.’
snp4.16:14.1:
He shouldn’t come under the sway
of anger or pride.
snp4.16:14.2:
Having dug up their root
he would stand firm.
snp4.16:14.3:
Then, when prevailing
—yes—
he’d prevail over notions of dear & undear.
snp4.16:15.1:
Deferring to discernment
enraptured with what’s admirable,
snp4.16:15.3:
should conquer
discontent
in his isolated spot,
snp4.16:15.4:
should conquer
these four
thoughts of lament:
snp4.16:16.1:
‘What will I eat,
or where will I eat?
snp4.16:16.2:
How badly I slept.
Tonight where will I sleep?’
snp4.16:16.3:
These lamenting thoughts
he should subdue—
one under training,
wandering without home.
snp4.16:17.1:
Receiving food & cloth
at appropriate times,
snp4.16:17.2:
he should have a sense of enough
for the sake of contentment.
snp4.16:17.3:
Guarded in regard to these things
going restrained into a village,
snp4.16:17.4:
even when harassed
he shouldn’t say a harsh word.
snp4.16:18.2:
committed to jhāna,
he should be continually wakeful.
snp4.16:18.4:
he should cut off any penchant
to conjecture or worry.
snp4.16:19.2:
should smash any rigidity
toward his fellows in the holy life;
snp4.16:19.3:
should utter skillful words
that are not untimely;
snp4.16:19.4:
should give no mind
to the gossip people might say.
snp4.16:20.1:
And then there are in the world
the five kinds of dust
snp4.16:20.2:
for whose subduing, mindful,
he should train:
snp4.16:21.1:
with regard to these things
he should subdue his desire.
snp4.16:21.2:
A monk, mindful,
his mind well released,
snp4.16:21.3:
contemplating the right Dhamma
at the right times,
snp4.16:21.4:
on coming
to oneness
should annihilate
darkness,”
the Blessed One said.
